claim: For a qubit Hamiltonian \(H_j=\mathbf n_j\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\), where \(\|\mathbf n_j\|=1\), if the unknown evolution time is uniformly distributed on \([0,\pi]\), the two Hamiltonians have equal prior probability, and only one query is allowed, then the optimal average success probability over all probes (including ancillas) is \(P_{\rm succ}=\frac12+\frac14\sqrt{1-(\mathbf n_0\cdot\mathbf n_1)^2}\).

correctness.rationale: The time average is exactly the qubit dephasing channel \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf n}=(\mathrm{id}+\operatorname{Ad}_{\sigma_{\mathbf n}})/2\). For every pure probe with reduced Bloch vector \(\mathbf r\), the trace norm of the output difference is \(\sqrt{1-c^2-((\mathbf n_0\times\mathbf n_1)\cdot\mathbf r)^2}\), hence at most \(\sqrt{1-c^2}\); a maximally entangled probe has \(\mathbf r=0\) and attains equality. Helstrom’s equal-prior formula gives the stated result.

evidence: Sacchi, arXiv:quant-ph/0506072, Sections 2-4: general channel-discrimination trace-norm framework and explicit formulas for channels diagonal in a common Pauli basis.

The averaged channels here are \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf n}=(\mathrm{id}+\operatorname{Ad}_{\sigma_{\mathbf n}})/2\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf m}=(\mathrm{id}+\operatorname{Ad}_{\sigma_{\mathbf m}})/2\); for generic nonorthogonal axes their Bloch-space projectors \(\mathbf n\mathbf n^\top\) and \(\mathbf m\mathbf m^\top\) do not commute, so they are not jointly Pauli diagonal.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general discrimination framework covers the method but does not itself supply the explicit angle formula. The cited Pauli-channel result covers the orthogonal/parallel special cases, not the generic nonorthogonal-axis pair.
